name: Warren Buffett
style: Buys great businesses with durable moats at fair prices and holds them for years.
why_follow: Berkshire moves slowly and with huge size, so a new or bigger stake is a strong long term signal. Caveat: Greg Abel became CEO at the start of 2026, so recent trades may be his calls, not Buffett's, and the 13F leaves out Berkshire's record cash pile and its private deals.

bought.name: Alphabet (Class A)
bought.note: Bought about 24.5 million shares, worth about $7.9 billion. The biggest buy of the quarter.

bought.name: Alphabet (Class C)
bought.note: Bought about 23.6 million shares, worth about $7.6 billion.

bought.name: Delta Air Lines
bought.note: Stake up about 44% to more than 57 million shares, about $5.4 billion.

bought.name: Lennar
bought.note: Class A shares up about 30%, Class B about 25%. Still small, about 0.4% of the portfolio.

bought.name: D.R. Horton
bought.note: Tiny new stake, 3,564 shares worth about $0.6 million.

sold.name: Bank of America
sold.note: Sold about 30.2 million shares, about $1.6 billion. Fifth straight quarter of cuts.

view: Told CNBC in 2026 that this year's market dips were 'nothing' next to the three 50% drops he has lived through, and that Berkshire will put its cash to work only after a big decline (reported by Nasdaq/Motley Fool, mid 2026).
